claims.text: Additive manufacturing combined with thermomechanical treatment can refine the grain structure of refractory high-entropy alloys.
A refined grain structure improves resistance to degradation in refractory high-entropy alloys.
A refined grain structure enhances the ductility of refractory high-entropy alloys.
A refined grain structure enhances the thermal stability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Grain refinement increases the strength of refractory high-entropy alloys relative to coarse-grained alloys.
Grain refinement increases the toughness of refractory high-entropy alloys relative to coarse-grained alloys.
The mechanical-performance improvement from grain refinement will persist under high-temperature conditions.
The mechanical-performance improvement from grain refinement will persist under irradiation conditions.
Refined-grain refractory high-entropy alloys will maintain thermal stability while achieving improved mechanical performance.
Refined-grain refractory high-entropy alloys will maintain irradiation stability while achieving improved mechanical performance.
There may be trade-offs between mechanical performance and thermal or irradiation stability.
The optimal additive-manufacturing and thermomechanical-treatment conditions are not yet fully understood.
The mechanisms underlying the proposed performance improvement are not yet fully understood.
